summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House):

blocks.text: The following analysis is based on draft bill text that was made available by the House of Representatives and may differ from the bill text as introduced.

This bill establishes an interagency task force to shut down criminal syndicates perpetuating mass online scams. This bill also explicitly authorizes sanctions against foreign individuals or entities operating or providing support to scam compounds. (Scam compounds target individuals for financial fraud and are concentrated in Southeast Asia.)

The President must establish an interagency task force to shut down transnational criminal syndicates that use large scam centers and forced labor of trafficked persons to perpetuate mass online scams against Americans. The task force must submit to Congress and oversee implementation of a strategy to combat scam centers, dismantle the criminal elements involved with them, and hold corrupt officials accountable. The task force must periodically report to Congress, including a list of foreign persons sanctioned by the United States for their involvement with online financial scams from Southeast Asia against U.S. nationals.

The President is explicitly authorized to impose visa- and property-blocking sanctions on (1) any foreign individual or entity that owns, controls, directs, or provides significant support to a significant scam compound operation or an enabling service; and (2) foreign government officials who knowingly enable or benefit from scam compound operations within their jurisdiction.

The Department of State is authorized to provide (1) trauma-informed care and other support services for trafficked persons within online scam centers, and (2) high-resolution satellite imagery to nongovernmental organizations and research institutions for the purposes of monitoring and documenting human rights abuses related to online scam centers in Southeast Asia.

The Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act would set up a government task force to shut down criminal groups that run large-scale online scams against Americans. These scams are often run from scam compounds, mainly in Southeast Asia, where people are targeted for financial fraud and where trafficked people are forced to work.

The President would have to create this interagency task force. It would be responsible for developing and overseeing a strategy to fight scam centers, take apart the criminal networks behind them, and hold corrupt officials accountable. The task force would have to report regularly to Congress, including a list of foreign individuals sanctioned by the United States for their part in online financial scams against U.S. nationals from Southeast Asia.

The bill would explicitly allow the President to impose visa and property-blocking sanctions in two situations. The first is against any foreign person or company that owns, controls, directs, or significantly supports a significant scam compound operation or a service that enables one. The second is against foreign government officials who knowingly enable or profit from scam compound operations in their jurisdiction.

The bill would also allow the Department of State to provide two kinds of help. It could offer trauma-informed care and other support services to trafficked people inside online scam centers. It could also give high-resolution satellite images to nongovernmental organizations and research institutions so they can monitor and document human rights abuses linked to these centers in Southeast Asia.
